analyst_view.overall: Early view: leaders Arsenal (27 points, five goals conceded in 10 games) host Marco Rose's Bournemouth, who are seventh and have won eight in a row in all competitions with Evanilson scoring in five straight league games. Both play in Europe that week: Arsenal host Real Madrid on Wednesday 9 December, while Bournemouth host Viktoria Plzen on the Thursday night and get less than three days to recover. Bukayo Saka (quad, hurt against Bayern in October) was expected to be out six weeks to two months, so his return around this date is uncertain.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.7 goals. I lean lower: Arsenal have the best defence in the league and their last two league wins were both 1-0, with Arteta asking for more chaos after a flat win over Hull. Bournemouth arrive on a short turnaround after a Thursday European game, which tends to blunt their pressing.

corners.text: The numbers say 10.1 corners. I lean slightly higher: Arsenal should have long spells of pressure against a tired Bournemouth side, and their wide play and set-piece routines tend to pile up corners in home games like this.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.3 cards. Nothing points clearly either way this far out: Bournemouth's aggressive pressing can bring bookings, but a side on short rest may drop deeper and press less. The referee is not yet known.

shots.text: The numbers say 25.5 shots. Arsenal should take most of them at home, but recent Arsenal games have been tight and low on clear chances, while Bournemouth's own output may fall after the Plzen game, so I stay close to the number.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 7.7 shots on target. I lean a little lower: Arsenal concede very few clean chances, and their recent 1-0 wins were short on quality in front of goal, especially with Saka's return still uncertain.
